Do not alter the runtime behaviour of the original test: the same methods must be called with the same arguments and produce the same expected outcomes.

The actual test only exercises three simple cases. Let me write a clean version.Compilation succeeded (`COMPILE_OK`). I improved understandability by removing the large block of dead code (unused `Stream<Arguments>` providers and helper methods never referenced by the test) and keeping only the single helper plus the three assertions, with a clear method name and a comment explaining the backwards-compatibility rationale. Runtime behavior is unchanged — `consumeCssIdentifier()` is still called with `"1"`, `"-"`, and `"-1"` and asserted against the same expected results.
